title: Act III, Scene III
focus: Romeo's despair in the Friar's cell

teacherSummary.text: Romeo hides in the Friar's cell, despairing at banishment. The Nurse arrives; Romeo draws a dagger to kill himself; the Friar stops him and lays out a plan: spend the night with Juliet, flee to Mantua, and wait until the marriage can be announced.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Ha, banishment! be merciful, say “death” slowly and put it in my own words: Romeo tells the Friar that exile is worse than death and begs him not to call it mercy. Next, craft. I notice the emotional outburst and his pleading repetition of the hated word "banished." The strongest word is “banishment”: it means exile from Verona, which separates him from Juliet. Then, effect. Why does Romeo think banishment is worse than death? My answer: Romeo thinks banishment is worse than death because exile means life without Juliet, so even a pardon from execution feels like torture; his despair shows how extreme and impulsive his emotions are.
